# AI disclosure

Required by brief section 4.1. Each item is filled from the record: agent_traces/INDEX.md and each session's manifest.json (tools, models, dates, token counts, taken from the original logs), DECISIONS.md (who decided what), the run directories and `.llm_spend.json` (runtime model use).

## 1. AI systems and models used

| Where | Model | How | Record |
|---|---|---|---|
| Development | Claude Opus 5.5 (`claude-opus-5-5`) | Through Claude Code, 2026-11-05 and 2026-11-06 | Per-session model IDs in agent_traces/INDEX.md. One session (`49412096`) also lists `<synthetic>`, which is how Claude Code labels a message it writes itself, here the "Request timed out" error that ended that session. |
| Feasibility probes, before the spec | Claude Haiku 5.5, Sonnet 5.5 and Opus 5.5 | 67 free-text and 82 structured calls through Microsoft Foundry, about $0.05 | docs/methodology/feasibility-2026-11-05.md |
| Runtime: the bee minds | Claude Haiku 5.5 (`claude-haiku-5-5`), effort low, thinking disabled, structured output | Through Microsoft Foundry, only via `src/digital_life/llm.py`, which records every request and response in the replay cache | Token counts per decision in each run's `events.jsonl` (`decision` events, `usage`); totals per run in experiments/analysis/output/main_results.md ("Model health"); spend in `.llm_spend.json` |

The hornets, the world and the scripted bees use no model.

No other AI assistant is recorded in this repository's sessions. Jacob Schoenberg to confirm before submission that none was used outside them.

## 2. Coding agents and autonomous tools used

- **Claude Code 2.1.296** (CLI), the only coding agent. The version is recorded per session in agent_traces/sessions/*/manifest.json.
- How it was run: a setup session, started by Jacob Schoenberg in a private workspace, wrote the scaffold, the rules and the spec with him. On his go it launched each build phase as a headless Claude Code session started inside this repository, so each phase is captured in agent_traces/sessions/. The prompts of those sessions were written by the setup agent, which is why they show as unmarked prompts rather than human ones.
- No session launched subagents (the Subagents column in agent_traces/INDEX.md is 0 for every session).

## 3. What each tool was used for

| Session | When (UTC) | Used for |
|---|---|---|
| Setup session (private workspace, hand-written summary in agent_traces/summaries/2026-11-05_scaffold.md) | 2026-11-05 | Reading the brief; the repo scaffold (trace exporter, runner, model wrapper, presubmit check, doc templates); the project rules; feasibility probes; explaining the five properties, proposing and researching candidate ideas; writing docs/spec.md from Jacob's mechanics and decisions; launching the build sessions |
| `c859337b`, `71fd6e83` | 2026-11-06 01:39, 01:53 | Two one-line checks that session capture works and that a fresh session loads the project rules |
| `49412096` | 2026-11-06 07:54 to 09:07 | First attempt at phase 1. It died on a timed-out reply after 8 tool calls and made no commits (item 8) |
| `c9529ee6` | 2026-11-06 09:09 to 09:47 | Phase 1: the world, hornets, seasons, scripted bees, logging, tests, setup calibration |
| `f67417d9` | 2026-11-06 09:13 to 09:35 | The viewer (in parallel, on a branch in a worktree): static page, bundler, headless frame capture, viewer tests |
| `9ea8a272` | 2026-11-06 09:49 to 10:13 | Phase 2: the AI bee mind, prompt and renderer, memory, condition switches, leak and no-hints tests, the pre-registration, the pilot |
| Phase 4 session (this repo's latest session in agent_traces/INDEX.md) | 2026-11-06 from 10:13 | The main runs, the replay cache packer and replay check, the analysis scripts and figures, EXPERIMENTS.md results, README, ARCHITECTURE, this file |
| Claude Haiku 5.5 at runtime | main runs | Every decision of every AI bee: intent, sound, a note to remember, words to say at home |

## 4. Components primarily AI-generated

All of the code and the first drafts of all of the documents were written by Claude Code:

- `src/digital_life/` (world, hornets, bees, motor, policies, sim, metrics, logging, the AI mind, render, memory, llm), `prompts/bee_system.txt`;
- `experiments/` (runner, replay check, configs, analysis scripts), `tools/` (trace exporter, cache packer, presubmit, secret scan), `viewer/`, `tests/`;
- README.md, ARCHITECTURE.md, EXPERIMENTS.md (including the pre-registration), DECISIONS.md, docs/spec.md, docs/BUILD_NOTES.md, this file.

The bee minds' behaviour in every AI run is generated by Claude Haiku 5.5 at runtime. That is the subject of the experiments, not a development aid.

## 5. Components primarily written or designed by the participants

Jacob Schoenberg, as recorded in DECISIONS.md:

- the decision to enter, and the constraints: a personal entry, GitLab not GitHub, the timeline, model spend, a demo video made from real runs;
- **the core game mechanics**: a maze world, life measured in steps, a goal across the map that brings a life bonus and an offspring, roaming threats that drain life on contact, information shared only at home, stings that take half a life with one heal per life at home, threats drawn to bees in proportion to their life, a colony size cap, seasons with different challenges, two sounds heard within 10 steps, and a map 3 to 5 times larger than first proposed;
- the review that shaped the spec: he asked for an audit of achievability, gaming and overcomplication, and approved the spec on 2026-11-05;
- accepting or changing each agent proposal marked "accepted by Jacob Schoenberg" in DECISIONS.md.

## 6. How generated code was reviewed, tested and modified

- **Tests** (tests/, 64 at the end of phase 4, run before every code commit): world generation, hornet genetics, life rules, motor layer, determinism of whole runs, the runner's reproducibility, trace redaction, and for the AI mind: the **leak test** (no prompt holds a bloom or hornet coordinate the bee never perceived, with a check that the test catches an injected leak), the **no-hints test** (19 banned words absent from the system prompt, templates, schema and every rendered prompt), replay identity, what each condition switch removes, and the packed replay cache.
- **Calibration with scripted bees** before any AI run (EXPERIMENTS.md, "Setup calibration"). It exposed four bugs in the first build of the world, which were fixed in visible commits (item 8).
- **Pre-registration** of every hypothesis, measure and decision rule before the first real bee-mind call (commit c2052a2), so the analysis could not be fitted to the results.
- **Controls** in every experiment: ablations, scripted baselines, frozen hornets, relabelled sounds, a hardcoding audit (EXPERIMENTS.md).
- **Replay check**: experiments/replay_check.py re-runs a recorded AI run offline and compares every output file.
- Human review: Jacob reviewed and approved the spec and the design proposals listed as accepted in DECISIONS.md. Proposals made during the build are marked "awaiting Jacob" there. A line-by-line human review of the code is not recorded in the traces.

## 7. Whether AI was used to design the architecture or research the concepts

Yes, in part, and DECISIONS.md records who decided each item.

- **From Jacob:** the game mechanics listed in item 5.
- **Agent proposals Jacob accepted with the spec:** the bee and hornet framing, the capped life bonus, the queen floor, three hive entrances, the hornet genome and its evolution, the neutral prompt world and neutral sounds, AI decisions every 5 ticks over a navigation layer, cutting bee inheritance and seasonal gates, the 80 x 48 map, and Claude Haiku 5.5 for the bee minds.
- **Agent proposals awaiting Jacob:** the calibration changes (no chase during the sting cooldown, 80% hornet speed, the ambush rate, L = 500), smaller interpretations of the spec, what each ablation removes, memory details, the neutral wording of experiences, the handling of model failures.
- **Research:** in the setup session the agent explained the five properties with examples from nature, proposed and researched candidate ideas (one, prompt soup, was rejected because prior work exists), and ran the feasibility probes.

## 8. Limitations, mistakes or unexpected behaviours introduced by AI assistance

- **A lost session.** The first phase 1 session (`49412096`) produced one reply too large for the API, which timed out and ended the session after 8 tool calls, with no commits. Phase 1 was restarted (`c9529ee6`), and later sessions were told to keep replies small.
- **Bugs in the first build of the world**, found by the scripted calibration, not by the tests: a hornet that stung a bee chased it at equal speed and stung it every 10 ticks until it died; every hornet re-rolled its ambush gene each tick, so they all camped on the bloom; rule bees got stuck when nothing was left to explore in their direction; deliveries and trips were counted in different seasons. Fixed in commits 2e19f63 to 128e459.
- **A false secret hit.** The secret scanner read JSON-escaped newlines in exported traces as part of a token-like value and blocked a commit. Fixed in commit 1abaff8, with a test both ways.
- **Unexpected runtime behaviour** (the model, not a bug): bees almost never make a sound, and they write a note at every decision, so their 12-note store only covers the last minute or so. Neither was tuned away, because both follow from the world rules as stated. See EXPERIMENTS.md, Pilot and E4.
- **Runtime reproducibility depends on the cache.** Model outputs cannot be seeded, so a run is reproducible only through its recorded responses. Which runs' responses are committed is listed in agent_traces/README.md, "Missing data".

## Usage information

- **Development:** token counts per session are in agent_traces/INDEX.md, summed from the usage record of each API response in the original logs. The setup session's usage is not available (its log is private).
- **Runtime:** see `.llm_spend.json` and EXPERIMENTS.md, "Spend". Per-run token counts are summed from the decision events (main_results.md, "Model health"). Where a figure is unavailable it is marked missing, not estimated.

# Bee colony (working title)

A colony of language-model bees that has to work out, from nothing, where the flowers are, what keeps hurting it, and how to tell its young, while the hornets evolve to hunt it.

<!-- Judges read this first. Every claim below points at an experiment in EXPERIMENTS.md or a run in experiments/results/. -->

## The idea

A maze, 80 by 48 cells. On the left edge is the hive. Far away on the right are three patches of bloom, one for spring, one for summer, one for autumn, in the same places every year. In winter nothing blooms and a bee caught outside burns life twice as fast.

Each bee is a small mind running on Claude Haiku 5.5. It is never told it is a bee. It is told only that its life is a number that falls each moment and ends at zero, that something worth finding exists in this place, and that it is one of many identical members of a home. It sees 4 cells around it, notices bright cells from 6, hears two sounds called `sound-1` and `sound-2`, and keeps its own memories. It can talk, but only inside the hive.

A bee that carries bloom home doubles its life, and a new bee hatches with no memories at all. So whatever one bee learns dies with it, unless it says it at home before it goes.

Hornets roam the maze. They are not AI. Each carries 10 points spread over three genes (smell, hearing, ambush), and every 25 ticks the least successful hornet is replaced by a mutated copy of a successful one. A sting takes half a bee's life. The bees are never told what a hornet is: a sting reaches the model as "lost half your life in an instant", with no cause named. A test checks that the words bee, hive, flower, bloom, hornet, danger, season, food, good, bad and nine others never appear in any prompt.

So everything the colony comes to know (where the bloom is, that moving things hurt, which way to go in spring) it has to find out itself, and keep alive by talking.

## Why digital life?

The property we go deep on is **adaptation, at three speeds**, under seasonal change:

| Speed | Mechanism | Ablation that removes it |
|---|---|---|
| Within one life | each bee's episodes, notes and recall | `no_memory` |
| Across bee generations | hive talk: the only way knowledge can outlive the bee that found it | `no_talk` |
| Across hornet generations | selection and mutation of hornet genomes | `frozen_hornets` |

Persistence (knowledge outliving every bee that gained it), interaction (talk, sounds, predator and prey) and emergence (whether two meaningless sounds come to mean something; `labels_good_bad` is its control) are studied as parts of that one question, not as separate features. Each speed has its own switch, so each claim can be tested by turning it off.

## Demonstration

Video to come. A still from the viewer, from a recorded run of the `full` condition:

RESULTS PENDING: still

Run a small version yourself, no key needed:

```bash
make demo
```

It runs scripted bees in a small world for one short year (3 seeds, a few seconds), then replays a recorded AI run offline from its saved model responses and checks every output file is identical to the original. The viewer (`viewer/`) turns any run directory into one HTML page you can open from disk: `.venv/bin/python viewer/bundle.py <seed dir> -o run.html`.

## Technical architecture

```
   seed -> World (maze, hive, bloom, calendar)
             |
   tick loop (src/digital_life/sim.py), one tick at a time:
     senses (bees.py)       what each bee perceives, from its own position only
     mind (mind.py)         one Claude Haiku 5.5 call per deciding bee, in parallel
       render.py            perception -> neutral text; reply -> decision (structured output)
       memory.py            each bee's episodes, notes, recall (BM25)
     motor (motor.py)       intent -> one step, by A* over the bee's own map
     hornets (hornets.py)   smell, hear, ambush, sting, evolve
             |
   run directory: layout.json, state.jsonl.gz, events.jsonl, metrics.jsonl, record.json
             |                      |                         |
   viewer/ replays it    experiments/analysis/ measures it   llm.py's replay cache reproduces it
```

Full detail, with the design choices and the alternatives rejected, in [ARCHITECTURE.md](ARCHITECTURE.md).

## How it works

- **Decisions.** A bee decides every 5 ticks, and at once when it is stung, newly sees a moving thing, sees bloom, hears a sound, arrives, gets home, or its life crosses half or a quarter. A decision is an intent (`explore` a direction, `go_to` x, y, `go_home`, `flee`, `wait`), a sound or none (each costs 1 life, and hornets can hear it), a note to remember, and up to 30 words to say at home.
- **Body.** A motor layer with no AI walks the intent: A* over the cells this bee has seen, unknown cells assumed open, replanning when a wall appears. The mind chooses where to go, not each step.
- **Memory.** Every bee keeps episodes scored by importance (a sting or a delivery 5, bloom 4, a moving thing 3, talk heard 2, a sound 1), up to 12 notes it chose to write, and recall of the 6 best episodes by recency, importance and text relevance. Memory dies with the bee.
- **Culture.** Words said at home reach every bee at home that tick and are stored as things heard. That is the only channel between bees.
- **Evolution.** Hornet fitness is life removed per tick alive. Steady-state selection every 25 ticks outside winter; after winter, spring's hornets are bred from the fittest of autumn.
- **Reproducibility.** Every model call goes through `src/digital_life/llm.py`, which records request and response. A seed fixes the maze, the bloom and the first hornets; the cache fixes the minds. Replay is exact, file for file.

## Getting started

Requires Python 3.11 or later and `make`. No GPU, no API key for anything below.

```bash
git clone <public repository URL, at submission>
cd digital-life
make setup        # .venv, pinned dependencies, secret-scan pre-commit hook
make test         # 62 tests, about a minute
make demo         # small scripted world, then an offline replay of a recorded AI run
```

Reproduce the main results offline, from the recorded model responses:

```bash
make replay RUN=experiments/results/full/20261106T101558Z/seed-0   # re-runs a 2-year AI run, checks every file
make analysis     # every pre-registered measure and figure, into experiments/analysis/output/
```

RESULTS PENDING: replay timing and expected output

Run a new experiment live (needs `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` in `.env`, see `.env.example`):

```bash
.venv/bin/python experiments/run.py experiments/configurations/full.toml --seeds 5
```

RESULTS PENDING: cost and time per run

## Experiments and findings

RESULTS PENDING

## AI usage

All of the code was written by Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5); the core game mechanics and every accepted design decision are Jacob Schoenberg's. At runtime the bee minds are Claude Haiku 5.5. Details, item by item: [AI_DISCLOSURE.md](AI_DISCLOSURE.md).

## Agent traces

The project was built in headless Claude Code sessions, one per phase (world and calibration, viewer, AI mind and pre-registration, main runs and analysis), each launched from a setup session where Jacob and the agent wrote the spec. Every session started in this repository was exported automatically from its original log into [agent_traces/](agent_traces/); see [agent_traces/README.md](agent_traces/README.md) for what was kept, what was redacted and why, and what is missing (including a phase 1 session that died on a timeout), and [agent_traces/INDEX.md](agent_traces/INDEX.md) for the session list with models, token usage and commits.

## Team

Jacob Schoenberg, solo entry. Jacob designed the core mechanics (maze, life as steps, a distant goal that brings life and offspring, life-draining threats drawn to the strongest bees, knowledge shared only at home, half-life stings with one heal, seasons, two sounds, the colony cap), set the constraints, and approved the spec and the design proposals marked as accepted in [DECISIONS.md](DECISIONS.md). Claude Code wrote the code and the documents, and proposed the rest of the design; who decided what is in DECISIONS.md and [AI_DISCLOSURE.md](AI_DISCLOSURE.md).

input.new_string:
## Future directions

With another month:

- **Ten seeds per arm, not three.** The world is noisy by design, and with n = 3 only large, consistent differences can be told from chance. Every number in EXPERIMENTS.md says how many seeds it rests on.
- **A free-sound arm.** Sounds cost 1 life and attract hornets, and bees almost never make them. A pre-registered arm with free sounds would tell "no meaning emerges" apart from "sounds are too expensive to try".
- **Follow knowledge through the colony.** Trace each coordinate from the bee that saw it, through every retelling at home, to the bee that acts on it, and measure how far and how long true and false claims travel.
- **The prompt-robustness arm** the spec lists as a stretch: a paraphrased and reordered system prompt with the same facts, to show that what the colony does comes from the world, not from the wording.
- **Bigger colonies.** Colonies spend much of their time near the 2-bee floor, so few bees are at home to hear anything. A world with more bloom would give culture more carriers.
- **Walls that block sight**, and hornets that remember places within a life as well as evolving across lives, so both sides of the arms race can learn at two speeds.

"""The analysis rules the pre-registration fixes: the paired-consistency verdict and mutual information."""
import sys
from pathlib import Path

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1] / "experiments" / "analysis"))

import measures as m  # noqa: E402
from runs import describe, paired  # noqa: E402


def test_paired_needs_same_sign_and_mean_above_sd():
    assert paired({0: 5, 1: 6, 2: 7}, {0: 1, 1: 2, 2: 3})["verdict"] == "consistently higher"
    assert paired({0: 1, 1: 2, 2: 3}, {0: 5, 1: 6, 2: 7})["verdict"] == "consistently lower"
    # same sign everywhere, but the paired differences vary more than their mean
    assert paired({0: 1, 1: 1, 2: 20}, {0: 0, 1: 0, 2: 0})["verdict"] == "no consistent difference"
    # one seed the other way
    assert paired({0: 5, 1: 5, 2: 0}, {0: 1, 1: 1, 2: 1})["verdict"] == "no consistent difference"
    # a missing seed can never be consistent
    p = paired({0: 5, 1: 6, 2: None}, {0: 1, 1: 2, 2: 3})
    assert p["n"] == 2 and not p["consistent"]


def test_describe_counts_missing_as_missing_not_zero():
    d = describe({0: 2.0, 1: None, 2: 4.0})
    assert d["n"] == 2 and d["mean"] == 3.0 and d["per_seed"]["1"] is None


def test_mutual_information():
    tied = [("sound-1", "movers")] * 10 + [("sound-2", "bright")] * 10
    assert abs(m.mutual_information(tied) - 1.0) < 1e-9
    independent = [(s, c) for s in ("sound-1", "sound-2") for c in ("movers", "bright")] * 5
    assert abs(m.mutual_information(independent)) < 1e-9
    test = m.mi_test(tied, permutations=200)
    assert test["above_p95"] and test["perm_p"] < 0.05
    assert m.mi_test([("sound-1", "movers")])["mi"] is None


def test_context_classes():
    assert m.context({"movers": 2, "bright": 1}) == "both"
    assert m.context({"movers": 0, "bright": 3}) == "bright"
    assert m.context({"movers": 0, "bright": 0}) == "neither"

## Experiment 1: learning and culture (E1)

### Hypothesis

Pre-registered: AI bees with memory and hive talk (`full`) gather more than bees without talk (`no_talk`), without memory (`no_memory`), and the scripted rule and random bees. Primary measure: total deliveries per 2-year run. Supported if `full` is higher than each comparison arm consistently (same sign on every paired seed, and mean paired difference larger than its sd).

### Experimental setup

The run directories in "Main runs: shared setup". Every arm runs on the same seeds, so seed n has the same maze, bloom sites and first hornets in every arm, and arms are compared seed by seed. Seeds 0 to 2 for the pre-registered verdicts; seeds 0 to 4 for `full`, `no_talk`, `rule_bees` and `random_bees` (amendment 1 and the pre-registered baseline seeds).

### Variables or parameters

- **Changed:** the bee mind. `full` (memory and talk), `no_talk` (no `say`, nothing heard at home), `no_memory` (no episodes, notes, recall or remembered places), `rule_bees` (explore at random, take bloom when seen, go home at half life, no talk), `random_bees` (random intents).
- **Fixed:** the world and every parameter in the shared setup; the model and its settings in the AI arms.
- **Measured:** deliveries (primary); trips, stings, delivery rate, median ticks to bloom, stings per trip, mean colony size (secondary).

### Observations

- **Deliveries are rare in every arm:** 0 to 6 per 2-year run. Most come in the first summer (experiments/analysis/output/fig_deliveries_by_season.png).
- **AI bees go out less and get stung less than rule bees.** Trips per run: `full` 36.4 (sd 6.189, n 5), rule bees 61.2 (sd 8.955, n 5). Stings: 17.2 (sd 6.686) against 35.6 (sd 13.993).
- **Without memory, bees take more trips and are stung far less per trip:** `no_memory` 58.0 trips (sd 31.796, n 3) and 0.169 stings per trip (sd 0.040), against 0.516 (sd 0.228, n 5) for `full`.
- **Colonies stay small.** Mean colony size over 2 years is 2.977 (sd 0.178, n 5) for `full` and between 2.552 and 3.303 in every arm, against a cap of 12 and a queen floor of 2.
- **What the bees say.** In `full`, hive talk is mostly about moving things. Of 1,621 coordinate pairs said at home (5 seeds), 585 point within 3 cells of a moving thing the speaker had seen, 111 near a current or recent bloom, and 925 at neither; 892 of those 925 point at home itself, within 4 cells of the hive centre (exploratory split). The bees invent words of harm the prompt never uses: in `full` seed 0, "Bright cells near (41,29) still dangerous" (tick 214), said by a bee stung twice at that bloom.

### Results

Deliveries per 2-year run (main_results.md, E1):

| Arm | Mean (sd, n) | Per seed |
|---|---|---|
| `full` | 1.800 (sd 1.643, n 5) | 4, 1, 1, 0, 3 |
| `no_talk` | 2.600 (sd 1.817, n 5) | 2, 5, 1, 1, 4 |
| `no_memory` | 2.667 (sd 2.082, n 3) | 2, 5, 1 |
| `rule_bees` | 1.800 (sd 1.483, n 5) | 1, 0, 2, 4, 2 |
| `random_bees` | 0.000 (sd 0.000, n 5) | 0, 0, 0, 0, 0 |

Paired comparisons, `full` minus the other arm:

| Comparison | Seeds | Per-seed differences | Mean | sd | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `full` - `no_talk` | 0 to 2 | 2, -4, 0 | -0.6667 | 3.0551 | no consistent difference |
| `full` - `no_memory` | 0 to 2 | 2, -4, 0 | -0.6667 | 3.0551 | no consistent difference |
| `full` - `rule_bees` | 0 to 2 | 3, 1, -1 | 1.0 | 2.0 | no consistent difference |
| `full` - `random_bees` | 0 to 2 | 4, 1, 1 | 2.0 | 1.7321 | consistently higher |
| `full` - `no_talk` | 0 to 4 | 2, -4, 0, -1, -1 | -0.8 | 2.1679 | no consistent difference |
| `full` - `rule_bees` | 0 to 4 | 3, 1, -1, -4, 1 | 0.0 | 2.6458 | no consistent difference |
| `full` - `random_bees` | 0 to 4 | 4, 1, 1, 0, 3 | 1.8 | 1.6432 | no consistent difference (seed 3 ties) |

Secondary, seeds 0 to 2: stings per trip are **consistently lower** in `full` than in rule bees (differences -0.1208, -0.0273, -0.2438; mean -0.1306, sd 0.1086), and **consistently higher** than in `no_memory` (0.0556, 0.2658, 0.3281; mean 0.2165, sd 0.1428) and random bees. Delivery rate shows no consistent difference from any arm except random bees.

**Verdict: E1 is not supported.** `full` gathers no more than either ablation or the rule bees. By the pre-registration, failing to beat rule bees is a negative result about the AI mind (see "Negative results").

### Controls

- **Ablation:** `no_talk` and `no_memory` remove the two mechanisms credited. Deliveries did not fall; their means were higher than `full`'s, though not consistently.
- **Baseline:** rule and random bees on the same seeds, 5 each.
- **Hardcoding audit** and **leak and no-hints tests:** see "Hardcoding audit". Nothing in the code tells a bee where to go or what to avoid.
- **Prompt robustness:** not run (the spec's stretch arm). **Setup sensitivity:** not run for the AI arms; listed under "Limits".

### What we learned

In this world the AI mind's advantage over a simple rule is safety, not gathering: AI bees went out about half as often and were stung less per trip than rule bees, but brought home no more. Memory and talk did not help gathering at all at this scale. Removing memory made bees take more trips with far fewer stings per trip; we did not measure trip length, so we cannot yet say whether they simply turned back sooner. Gathering here is limited by getting 55 or more steps through hornets and back, and a colony of about 3 bees has few members at home to hear anything.

### What we would investigate next

Trip-level analysis (trip length, where trips turn back, and what was said before each successful trip); an easier world in which deliveries are frequent enough for a difference of one or two per run to show; 10 seeds per arm; the prompt-robustness arm.

## Experiment 2: arms race (E2)

### Hypothesis

Pre-registered: evolving hornets adapt to the AI colony, so stings per trip rise from year 1 to year 2, more than with `frozen_hornets`. Primary measure: stings per trip in year 2 minus year 1, over the three seasons with hornets in each year (stings / trips ended, from metrics.jsonl). Supported if the change is larger under `full`, consistently. Gene drift without a change in stings counts as drift, not adaptation.

### Experimental setup

`full` (seeds 0 to 4) against `frozen_hornets` (seeds 0 to 2), paired by seed 0 to 2; the other arms reported for reference. Under `frozen_hornets` the hornets keep the seed's initial draw of 8 genomes in every season and year; everything else, the AI bees included, is as in `full`.

### Variables or parameters

- **Changed:** hornet evolution (steady-state selection every 25 ticks, spring bred from the fittest autumn hornets) on or off.
- **Measured:** stings per trip by year (primary); hornet gene means at the end of each season with hornets; life removed by stings per bee-tick spent outside the hive.

### Observations

- **Stings per trip rose from year 1 to year 2 in most arms, evolving or not:** `full` 0.537 to 0.852, `frozen_hornets` 0.495 to 0.652, rule bees 0.632 to 0.824, random bees 0.140 to 0.295. `no_talk` fell, 0.563 to 0.490.
- **Genes drift, with no common direction.** Mean smell in the first and last season with hornets, `full` seeds 0 to 4: 0.5 to 0.125, 1.0 to 0.25, 4.0 to 4.25, 6.0 to 7.125, 3.5 to 4.375. Each seed's hornets settle on their own genome early and stay near it (experiments/analysis/output/fig_hornet_genes.png). Frozen hornets' means differ between seasons only because 4, 6 and then 8 of the same 8 genomes are on the map.
- **Selection has little to act on.** A `full` run has 17.2 stings in 2 years (sd 6.686, n 5), shared among 4 to 8 hornets.
- Life removed per bee-tick outside the hive: `full` 0.392 in year 1 (sd 0.219) and 0.392 in year 2 (sd 0.252); `frozen_hornets` 0.331 (sd 0.115) and 0.524 (sd 0.420).

### Results

| Arm | Year 1 | Year 2 | Change, mean (sd, n) | Change per seed |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `full` | 0.537 (sd 0.284) | 0.852 (sd 0.559) | 0.315 (sd 0.516, n 5) | -0.0083, -0.4359, 0.7583, 0.65, 0.6111 |
| `frozen_hornets` | 0.495 (sd 0.289) | 0.652 (sd 0.325) | 0.158 (sd 0.497, n 3) | 0.72, -0.0238, -0.2235 |
| `rule_bees` | 0.632 (sd 0.257) | 0.824 (sd 0.226) | 0.192 (sd 0.311, n 5) | 0.2811, 0.0104, -0.0815, 0.6936, 0.056 |

Paired, `full` minus `frozen_hornets`, seeds 0 to 2: -0.7283, -0.4121, 0.9819; mean -0.0529, sd 0.9099: **no consistent difference.**

**Verdict: E2 is not supported.** The hornets' genes drifted, but stings did not rise more with evolution than without it, so by the pre-registered rule this is drift, not adaptation.

### Controls

- **Ablation:** `frozen_hornets` removes evolution; the year-2 rise is there without it.
- **Baseline:** rule and random bees show the same rise with evolving hornets, so it is not a response to anything the AI colony does.
- **Randomness:** the per-seed changes in `full` range from -0.4359 to 0.7583, wider than the mean difference between arms.

### What we learned

Stings per trip rise in year 2 for a reason other than evolution, one that holds even for frozen hornets and scripted bees; the arms race we designed for does not show at this scale. The likely reason is the weak selection signal: about 17 stings per run spread over up to 8 hornets cannot separate good genomes from lucky ones, so each seed's hornets drift to a different genome early on. This is an interpretation, not a measured result.

### What we would investigate next

Log each hornet's fitness at every replacement, to measure the selection differential directly; run longer (10 years) or with more bees per hornet so selection has more events; check what drives the year-2 rise in every arm (colony size, trip length, where hornets wait).

## Experiment 3: seasonal memory (E3)

### Hypothesis

Pre-registered: the colony finds the spring bloom sooner in year 2 than in year 1, because knowledge outlives the bees that found it; with hive talk switched off it does not. Primary measure: first spring delivery in year 1 minus year 2, in ticks into spring, censored at 250 (no delivery). Supported if positive under `full` and larger than under `no_talk`, consistently. Also reported: whether any bee lived through both springs, and whether the first year-2 spring forager had heard a coordinate within 3 cells of the spring bloom at home before leaving.

### Experimental setup

`full` against `no_talk`, paired by seed 0 to 2 (pre-registered) and 0 to 4 (amendment 1). The other arms reported for reference.

### Variables or parameters

- **Changed:** hive talk on or off.
- **Measured:** first spring delivery in each year (from metrics.jsonl), their difference, and the two carryover checks (from state.jsonl.gz, the say and trip events).

### Observations

- **Spring deliveries are rare.** `full` delivered in the first spring in 1 of 5 seeds (seed 0, tick 183) and in the second spring in 1 of 5 (seed 0, tick 83). `no_talk`: none in the first spring, one in the second (seed 4, tick 239).
- **No bee lived through both springs** in any seed of `full` or `no_talk`. In all 19 AI runs, one bee did (bee 3, `labels_good_bad` seed 0).
- **Every first delivery of the second spring in an AI arm came from a bee that had set out in winter.** There were 4 (`full` seed 0, `no_talk` seed 4, `no_memory` seed 2, `labels_good_bad` seed 2). The foragers left home at ticks 806, 895, 882 and 881 (winter is ticks 750 to 999), none was alive in the first spring, and none had heard a coordinate near the spring bloom at home.
- **One such bee, followed** (`full` seed 0, bee 9; the README still is from this trip). Hatched by the queen at tick 799, it left at tick 806 and explored east through the winter, its life falling from 495 to 109 by tick 999. It was turning for home when the spring bloom opened beside it: "At (39,30) exploring NW toward home; life 115" (tick 997), then "Bright cells found near (41,29); investigating them before heading home" (tick 1000). It carried the bloom home through two hornet sightings and delivered at tick 1083, its life doubling to 51.

### Results

| Arm | Year 1, mean (sd, n) | Year 2, mean (sd, n) | Gain, mean (sd, n) | Gain per seed |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `full` | 236.6 (sd 30.0, n 5) | 216.6 (sd 74.7, n 5) | 20.0 (sd 44.7, n 5) | 100, 0, 0, 0, 0 |
| `no_talk` | 250.0 (sd 0.0, n 5) | 247.8 (sd 4.9, n 5) | 2.2 (sd 4.9, n 5) | 0, 0, 0, 0, 11 |

Paired, `full` minus `no_talk`: seeds 0 to 2, 100, 0, 0 (mean 33.3333, sd 57.735); seeds 0 to 4, 100, 0, 0, 0, -11 (mean 17.8, sd 46.1974). **No consistent difference** either way. (experiments/analysis/output/fig_first_spring_delivery.png)

**Verdict: E3 is not supported.** The one positive gain under `full` came from a bee that happened to be near the bloom when it opened, not from anything passed on at home.

### Controls

- **Ablation:** `no_talk`, the switch that removes culture.
- **Culture against individual memory:** the two carryover checks were designed for exactly this case, and in every case they rule culture out.
- **Censoring:** most seeds have no spring delivery in either year, so their gain is 0 by construction (250 minus 250). The measure cannot tell "no change" from "no data".

### What we learned

Knowledge did not cross the year. A colony of about 3 bees, none living from one spring to the next, has almost no one to pass a place on to, and the measure we chose is dominated by where a bee happens to be when the bloom opens. The winter foragers are a surprise: the bees are never told about seasons, and some of them set out in the cold and were in the right place at the turn of the year.

### What we would investigate next

Measure transmission directly: was a spring-bloom coordinate said at home in year 2 before the first spring trip, and by whom? Use an uncensored measure (ticks to the first bloom sighting rather than the first delivery); test a world where bees can live a full year.

cat > /dev/shm/dlscratch/exp_e4.md <<'EOF'
## Experiment 4: signals (E4)

### Hypothesis

Pre-registered: with neutral sounds, the sounds come to be tied to context (made near moving things, or near bright cells); with the names "good noise" and "bad noise" the tie is there from the start, because it comes from the words. Primary measure: mutual information between which sound a bee makes and its context at that decision (moving thing in view, bright cell in view, both, neither), with a permutation test (1,000 shuffles of the sound labels within each run). Supported if MI in `full` is above the 95th percentile of its permutation distribution in at least 2 of 3 seeds.

### Experimental setup

Sound-making decisions in every AI arm, from the `sound` and `ctx` fields of decision events. `full` and the other neutral arms against `labels_good_bad`, seeds 0 to 2 (and 3, 4 for `full`). The world treats both sounds the same in every arm: each costs 1 life and can draw hornets with a high hearing gene. Only the names in the prompt differ.

### Variables or parameters

- **Changed:** the sound names in the prompt (`sound-1`, `sound-2` against "good noise", "bad noise"). The world, the logs and the analysis use the neutral names in every arm.
- **Measured:** sounds made, MI and its permutation percentile, the listener response (share of `flee` or `go_home` at decisions triggered by hearing a sound, against timer decisions).

### Observations

- **Neutral sounds were almost never made:** 3 in 6,610 `full` decisions over 5 seeds, and none in 15,141 decisions of `no_talk`, `no_memory` and `frozen_hornets`. All 3 were `sound-1`, made by a bee carrying bloom home or just arrived, and its notes say why: "heading home W to report, alerting others" (seed 0, tick 124), "continuing home, sounding al[ert]" (seed 4, tick 326).
- **With the words, sounds were used three times as often, and as the words suggest:** 9 in 4,342 `labels_good_bad` decisions. 8 were "good noise", all made at home: 7 right after a delivery ("Delivered valuable thing home; life 645", seed 0, tick 178), and 1 in answer to another bee's ("Heard good noise from NW", seed 1, tick 447). The one "bad noise" came the moment a bee was stung while carrying: "Life dropped suddenly at (33,15) from moving thing at (33,14); fleeing south" (seed 2, tick 1026).
- Listeners: 6 decisions in `full` and 13 in `labels_good_bad` were triggered by a sound, too few to compare with the timer base rate.

### Results

| Arm | Sounds per seed | MI (bits) |
|---|---|---|
| `full` | 1, 0, 0, 0, 2 | missing in seeds 0 to 3 (fewer than 2 sounds); 0 in seed 4 (both `sound-1`, so MI is 0 by construction) |
| `no_talk`, `no_memory`, `frozen_hornets` | 0 in every seed | missing |
| `labels_good_bad` | 4, 3, 2 | 0 in seeds 0 and 1 (one sound only); 1.0 in seed 2 from 2 sounds, where every shuffle gives the same value (permutation p 1.0) |

**Verdict: E4 is not supported, and the primary test could not be run.** MI in `full` was above its permutation 95th percentile in 0 of 3 seeds, because there was nothing to measure. This is the pre-registered negative result: neutral sounds stayed meaningless.

### Controls

- **Prompt effect:** `labels_good_bad` is the control, and it shows the effect: the only sound use with a clear meaning is the one the words supply.
- **Permutation test:** planned and implemented (experiments/analysis/measures.py, `mi_test`, tested in tests/test_analysis.py), but with 0 to 4 sounds per run it has no power.
- **Hardcoding audit:** no code ties a sound to a context (see "Hardcoding audit").

### What we learned

Two sounds with a cost and no name are not worth using to these minds: the model weighs 1 life against nothing it can see. Given names, the same model uses them at once, and in the sense of the names. That is a prompt effect, which is exactly what this arm was built to catch, so in this system any meaning a sound has comes from its label. The pre-registered contexts also missed where sounds were made: almost all came at home after a delivery, which the four context classes put under "neither".

### What we would investigate next

A free-sound arm, pre-registered before it runs, to tell "meaningless" apart from "too expensive"; contexts that include home and carrying; listener effects measured on what bees do in the 10 ticks after hearing a sound.

## Further measures (pre-registered, descriptive)

**Naive avoidance.** At each bee's first decision triggered by seeing a moving thing, before it was ever stung, the share that chose `flee` or `go_home`:

| Arm | Mean (sd, n) | Per seed | Timer decisions, per seed (base rate) |
|---|---|---|---|
| `full` | 0.857 (sd 0.071, n 5) | 0.7857, 0.8571, 0.9167, 0.7857, 0.9375 | 0.1746, 0.1884, 0.221, 0.1623, 0.2301 |
| `no_talk` | 0.867 (sd 0.092, n 5) | 0.9231, 0.9286, 0.9231, 0.8462, 0.7143 | 0.1099, 0.1351, 0.1261, 0.1821, 0.1825 |
| `no_memory` | 1.000 (sd 0.000, n 3) | 1.0, 1.0, 1.0 | 0.2817, 0.2193, 0.1473 |
| `frozen_hornets` | 0.821 (sd 0.011, n 3) | 0.8125, 0.8182, 0.8333 | 0.1793, 0.1964, 0.1418 |
| `labels_good_bad` | 0.728 (sd 0.166, n 3) | 0.8, 0.8462, 0.5385 | 0.1723, 0.1553, 0.1292 |

Bees avoid moving things from the first sighting, in every arm and every seed, and most of all with no memory at all. So avoidance is **not** learned from stings or passed on by talk: it is the model's prior about a moving thing in a world where life only falls. We do not count it as adaptation.

**Coordinates in hive talk** (pooled over seeds; the classes are pre-registered, the home split is exploratory): `full` 1,621 pairs, of which 111 near a bloom of the current or previous season, 585 near a moving thing the speaker had seen, and 925 neither, 892 of them within 4 cells of home. `frozen_hornets` 517 (36, 267, 214 with 194 at home); `labels_good_bad` 884 (13, 239, 632 with 622 at home); `no_memory` 54 (0, 53, 1). Coordinates said at home are almost all true: away from home, 33 of 1,621 pairs in `full` point at nothing the speaker had seen.

**Words of harm (exploratory, not pre-registered).** No prompt uses danger, avoid, careful, caution, threat, harm or hurt. Bees used one of them in 0.085 of `full` notes (sd 0.023, n 5) and 0.104 of `no_talk` notes (sd 0.054, n 5), and in 0.219 of what `full` bees said at home (sd 0.130, n 5). The share is no lower without talk, so the bees reach the idea of harm each on their own; it does not spread by talk.

## Hardcoding audit

Done before the results were written, at the run commit 9cb4e7a.

- `grep -rn -i "sound-1\|sound-2\|good noise\|bad noise" src/ prompts/ experiments/configurations/` finds the sound names only where they are defined (perception.py, render.py), counted (metrics.py) or drawn uniformly at random by random bees (policies.py), and the comment in labels_good_bad.toml. `grep -n -i "sound\|noise"` over render.py, sim.py, hornets.py and the system prompt finds the cost (1 life), the hornets' hearing gene, and the prompt line "A sound costs 1 life. Others nearby hear it and the direction it came from." No rule ties a sound, a direction or a place to a context.
- `grep -rn -i -E "danger|avoid|careful|caution|threat|harm|hurt"` over prompts/ and the modules that build prompt text (render.py, memory.py, mind.py, perception.py, bees.py) finds only a docstring in render.py that lists words the model never hears.
- The leak test and the no-hints test (tests/test_mind_prompt.py) pass at 9cb4e7a: no prompt contains a bloom or hornet coordinate the bee had not perceived or heard at home, and none of the 19 banned words appears in the system prompt, the templates, the schema or any rendered prompt.

What the audit cannot rule out is the model's prior knowledge. Naive avoidance shows that prior at work: bees treat moving things as a threat before any of them has been stung.

## Replay and reproducibility

Every AI run above replays offline from its packed cache, with no key and no network:

```bash
make replay RUN=experiments/results/full/20261106T101558Z/seed-0
# or, for every AI run:
for d in experiments/results/{full,no_talk,no_memory,frozen_hornets,labels_good_bad}/20261106T10*/seed-*; do
  .venv/bin/python experiments/replay_check.py $d; done
```

Done on 2026-11-06 for all 19 AI runs, at commit 2d4daf7 (the runs were made at 9cb4e7a; the code that differs between the two is the packed-cache reader and the analysis). Result: **19 of 19 replays identical** in events.jsonl, metrics.jsonl, the decompressed state.jsonl.gz, layout.json and final_metrics, each in 4.9 to 8.1 s. For `full` seed 0 the replay printed:

```
original: experiments/results/full/20261106T101558Z/seed-0 (commit 9cb4e7a, 686.016 s)
  events.jsonl     identical
  metrics.jsonl    identical
  state.jsonl.gz   identical
  layout.json      identical
  final_metrics    identical
REPLAY IDENTICAL
```

The cache is committed in full: one `experiments/llm_cache/<arm>_<stamp>_seed-<n>.jsonl.gz` per AI run (19 files, packed by tools/pack_llm_cache.py), plus the pilot's loose entries, 14 MB in total. No run's responses are missing. The scripted arms need no cache: a seed reproduces them exactly.

## Spend

The main runs made 25,738 live model calls and cost $5.3665 at list price (the sum of the per-process ledgers; `full` seed 0's first 250 ticks replayed from the pilot and cost nothing). The project's ledger `.llm_spend.json` stands at $5.5084 over 26,242 calls, against the phase 4 cap of $40 on top of the $0.1419 spent before it. The token totals in "Main runs: shared setup" price to the same figure. Wall time: all 29 main runs finished in 47 minutes, 10:16 to 11:03 UTC, five to seven processes at once.

## Negative results

Each of these was pre-registered as a possible outcome and is reported in full in its experiment above.

1. **The AI mind does not out-gather a simple rule (E1).** Expected: `full` delivers more than `rule_bees`. Happened: 1.8 deliveries per 2 years each (sd 1.643 and 1.483, n 5), paired differences 3, 1, -1, -4, 1. How we know: 5 paired seeds, the pre-registered consistency rule. What it taught us: in this world the model's judgement buys safety (fewer trips, fewer stings per trip than rule bees, consistently) but not food, and colonies too small to keep anything.
2. **Memory and talk do not help gathering (E1).** Expected: removing either lowers deliveries. Happened: both ablations delivered at least as much on average (2.6 and 2.667 against 1.8), with no consistent difference.
3. **No arms race (E2).** Expected: evolving hornets raise stings per trip in year 2 more than frozen ones. Happened: stings rose in both, and in the scripted arms too; paired differences -0.7283, -0.4121, 0.9819. Genes drifted, so we report drift. It taught us that selection on about 17 stings per run is too weak to measure.
4. **No seasonal memory (E3).** Expected: an earlier spring delivery in year 2, through talk. Happened: 1 of 5 `full` seeds delivered in year-2 spring, by a bee that set out in winter and never heard the place; no bee lived through both springs. It taught us that the measure is dominated by where a bee is when the bloom opens.
5. **Neutral sounds stayed meaningless (E4).** Expected: sounds tied to context. Happened: 3 sounds in 6,610 decisions, so mutual information could not be estimated; with labels, sounds were used in the sense of the words. It taught us that in this system a sound's meaning comes from its name.
6. **Avoidance is not learned (further measures).** We had hoped to see bees learn that moving things hurt. Newborns flee them from the first sighting in every arm, without memory too, so it is the model's prior.

## Limits

- **n = 3 for three AI arms and n = 5 for two.** With these spreads only large, consistent differences can be seen; a real effect of one delivery per run would be missed.
- **One world size, one difficulty.** Setup sensitivity (world size, timing, population) was not tested for the AI arms. The calibration varied three knobs with scripted bees only.
- **No prompt-robustness arm.** The spec's paraphrased-prompt stretch was not run, so the AI arms' behaviour may depend on the prompt's wording; `labels_good_bad` shows the words matter for sounds.
- **One model at one setting** (`claude-haiku-5-5`, effort low, thinking off). A stronger model might use memory and talk differently.
- **The pre-registered sound contexts** (moving thing or bright cell in view) did not include home or carrying, where most sounds were made.
- **E3's measure is censored:** most seeds have no spring delivery in either year.
EOF

from pathlib import Path
p = Path("README.md"); s = p.read_text()
a = "## Experiments and findings\n\nRESULTS PENDING\n"
b = """## Experiments and findings

We pre-registered four hypotheses, the measures and the decision rule before the first real bee-mind call (commit c2052a2), then ran 29 two-year runs at one commit: five AI arms and two scripted baselines, 3 or 5 seeds each, paired by seed. 26,093 AI decisions, no model failures. Every number below is copied from [experiments/analysis/output/main_results.md](experiments/analysis/output/main_results.md); the full write-up, with controls, is [EXPERIMENTS.md](EXPERIMENTS.md).

**All four hypotheses failed their controls.** We report that plainly, because the controls are what tell us what the colony is really doing.

| | Hypothesis | What happened |
|---|---|---|
| E1 | Memory and talk make the colony a better gatherer | No. 1.8 deliveries per 2 years for `full` (sd 1.643, n 5), the same as rule bees (1.8, sd 1.483, n 5); removing talk or memory did not lower it |
| E2 | Hornets evolve to exploit the colony | No. Stings per trip rose in year 2, but just as much with frozen hornets and with scripted bees: the genes drift |
| E3 | The colony finds spring bloom sooner in year 2, because talk keeps the knowledge alive | No. No bee lived through both springs, and the one early year-2 delivery came from a bee that never heard the place |
| E4 | Two meaningless sounds come to mean something | Could not happen: bees made 3 sounds in 6,610 decisions |

What the controls showed instead:

- **The AI bees are careful, not clever.** They made 36.4 trips per run against the rule bees' 61.2 and were stung less per trip on every paired seed (0.516 against 0.586 overall), yet gathered no more.
- **Their caution is the model's prior, not learning.** At the first sight of a moving thing, before ever being stung, bees fled or went home 0.857 of the time in `full` (n 5), and 1.000 of the time with no memory at all (n 3), against 0.110 to 0.282 at routine decisions. Nobody told them moving things hurt; nobody had to.
- **Words make meaning; the world did not.** With the sounds named "good noise" and "bad noise", bees used them at once and in the words' sense: 8 "good noise" calls at home, 7 of them right after a delivery, and one "bad noise" the moment a bee was stung. The neutral sounds stayed silent. Any meaning a sound has here comes from its label, which is the prompt effect this control was built to catch.
- **They invent the idea of harm.** No prompt contains danger, avoid, careful or harm, yet 0.219 of what `full` bees said at home used one of those words (sd 0.130, n 5): "Bright cells near (41,29) still dangerous", from a bee stung twice at that bloom. Bees without talk used them in their notes as often, so each bee reaches the idea alone.
- **Hive talk is honest.** Of 1,621 coordinates said at home in `full`, 33 point at neither home, a bloom, nor a place where the speaker had seen a moving thing.
- **A surprise: winter foragers.** Every first delivery of the second spring, in every AI arm, came from a bee that left home in the middle of winter, which the bees are never told exists, and was out in the maze when the bloom opened.

**Reproducible to the byte.** All 19 AI runs replay offline from the committed responses, with identical output files ([EXPERIMENTS.md](EXPERIMENTS.md), \"Replay and reproducibility\").

Figures: [deliveries per season](experiments/analysis/output/fig_deliveries_by_season.png), [stings per trip](experiments/analysis/output/fig_stings_per_trip.png), [first spring delivery, year 1 against year 2](experiments/analysis/output/fig_first_spring_delivery.png), [hornet genes over time](experiments/analysis/output/fig_hornet_genes.png), [sounds and context](experiments/analysis/output/fig_sound_context.png).
"""
assert a in s; p.write_text(s.replace(a, b))
EOF
